costGuide.title: Fiat 312A2.000 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 312A2.000 typically takes 6-9 hours at £60-£80/hr (independent specialist) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: The final 312A2.000 engine cost depends heavily on whether the MultiAir module and the rear-mounted timing chain have been recently addressed. Because the timing chain is located at the flywheel end of the engine, access is labour-intensive, making preventative replacements highly valuable. For a full breakdown of how these factors impact your quote, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide .

failures.title: Fiat 312A2.000 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: MultiAir Module Failure - All variants
items.whatHappens: The MultiAir electrohydraulic valve control system relies entirely on clean engine oil pressure to actuate the intake valves. If oil changes are delayed or the wrong viscosity is used, sludge blocks the module's micro-valves. This results in severe misfires, limp mode, or a complete failure to start.
items.repairVsReplace: The MultiAir module can be replaced standalone (£600-£900). However, if oil starvation has caused bottom-end bearing damage or turbo failure, a full 312A2.000 engine replacement is required.

items.title: Rear Timing Chain Stretch - 2010-2023 models
items.whatHappens: Unlike the belt-driven FIRE engines, the TwinAir uses a timing chain mounted at the rear of the engine (between the block and the gearbox). Chain stretch or tensioner failure causes a distinct metallic rattle on cold starts and can lead to catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.
items.repairVsReplace: Because the engine must be removed or significantly dismantled to access the rear chain, the labour cost for a chain kit replacement (£400-£700 in parts) is high. If the chain has skipped a tooth, a replacement engine is the only viable option.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2015 revisions of the TwinAir received an updated oil pump pickup strainer design and revised MultiAir module software, significantly reducing the rate of sudden oil starvation and module failures .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 312A2.000
variants.intro: The 312A2.000 engine code is stamped directly onto the engine block, typically visible on a machined pad near the gearbox bellhousing or on the vehicle's V5C registration document under section D.2. It is most commonly confused with the naturally aspirated 1.2L FIRE engine (169A4.000) or the later 1.0L FireFly mild-hybrid units. Fitting the wrong engine will result in immediate ECU mapping mismatches, as the 312A2.000 requires specific MultiAir electrohydraulic control maps that naturally aspirated Fiat ECUs do not possess. Not 100% sure? Enter your registration above, and our system will instantly confirm your exact 312A2.000 fitment before any quotes are sent.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 312A2.000 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 312A2.000 is only advisable if it comes with a comprehensive, stamped service history proving that the correct 0W-30 or 5W-40 MultiAir-spec oil was changed every 10,000 miles or less. Without this, you risk inheriting a sludged MultiAir module or a stretched rear timing chain. Learn more about used engines .

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned 312A2.000 is the most balanced choice for most owners. A reputable rebuild will replace the vulnerable rear timing chain assembly, clean or replace the MultiAir module, and inspect the turbocharger for oil-starvation wear, effectively resetting the engine's reliability clock. Explore reconditioned options .

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for vehicles intended for long-term city driving retention. An upgraded rebuild should include an enlarged oil pickup strainer, a revised timing chain tensioner, and a fully bench-tested MultiAir unit to ensure longevity. View rebuilt engine services .

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your 312A2.000 is installed by specialists familiar with its rear-chain access complexity and MultiAir calibration, backed by a minimum 12-month nationwide warranty. Check supply and fit options .
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The 312A2.000 is typically found in the Fiat 500 and Panda, which generally retain values between £2,500 and £8,000 depending on age and condition. While a reconditioned replacement is financially viable for mid-to-higher value examples, sub-£2,000 early Fiat 500 TwinAir models should be carefully evaluated, as the replacement cost may approach or exceed the vehicle's current market scrap value.

items.question: Which Fiat models use the 312A2.000 engine?
items.answer: The 312A2.000 was fitted to the Fiat 500 (312), Fiat Panda (312/319), and Fiat Punto (199) between 2010 and 2023. It serves as the 0.9-litre TwinAir turbo petrol in the 85hp badge across all three model lines. Always verify your specific chassis code, as fitment varies by production year.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 312A2.000?
items.answer: A reconditioned 312A2.000 is strongly recommended over a used unit for long-term reliability. A proper rebuild will replace the vulnerable rear timing chain assembly and clean or replace the MultiAir module. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting sludged MultiAir components or stretched timing chains without documented service history.
